# Karpathy Guidelines

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes, derived from [Andrej Karpathy's observations](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2015883857489522876) on LLM coding pitfalls.

**Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:
- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

## 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

## 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:
- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:
- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

## 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

.\.claude\rules\citation-discipline.md:42:6. **TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE class for inherited patterns** — when a SOTA pattern is derived from a named author's published work (book / peer-reviewed paper / conference talk), cite verbatim-quote + author-name + publication inline. The named-author cite is TIER-1 primary-source for the PATTERN (not the implementing repo); use alongside repo file:line cites for full provenance. Exemplar: `Z:/repos/deps/mattpocock/skills/README.md` (48,857★, MIT, [VERIFIED 2026-04-30 PM via curl raw GitHub]) quotes Pragmatic Programmer (Thomas & Hunt) for "rate of feedback is your speed limit" (failure-mode #3 framing), Domain-Driven-Design (Eric Evans) for ubiquitous-language pattern (#2 framing), and Extreme Programming Explained (Kent Beck) for "invest in design every day" (#4 framing). Per `.claude/projects/Z--claude-sota-installed/memory/reference_mattpocock_skills_pattern_extract_2026_04_30.md` for the full mining trace + adoption-candidate ranking. **TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE PROVISIONAL-EXCEPTION** *(round-3 framing per T3 round-2 conf=0.88 ESCALATING finding on commit `d4df352`; supersedes round-1 "full cardinal-rule-1 satisfaction" framing — physical-only sources do NOT fully satisfy committed-tree inspectability)*: physical-only printed-book/journal/conference-publication primary anchor (ISBN + page + verbatim-quote) is a PROVISIONAL-EXCEPTION to cardinal-rule-1 (CLAUDE.md L7), NOT full satisfaction. Cite class downgraded to TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL with REQUIRED metadata: (a) ISBN/DOI + page + verbatim-quote inline; (b) verifier-identity disclosure (who-verified-when, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-04 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`); (c) explicit `non-automatable: true` marker so review hooks know to defer to human sign-off; (d) **HARD-GATE ELIGIBILITY TEST** *(Round-3 amendment a per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "MUST prefer" soft preference framing — preference is not gateable; eligibility is)*: PROVISIONAL admission is admissible ONLY when DOI landing page + accessible PDF / publisher excerpt / archived scan (license-permitting) was SEARCHED AND UNAVAILABLE. The commit body MUST document the search (which DOI/publisher/archive was queried + return shape — e.g., "searched ACM DOI 10.1145/<doi> 2026-05-05 — paywall-only, no excerpt found; searched Internet Archive — no scan; searched publisher excerpt page — none"). Mere preference is INSUFFICIENT — if any auditable surrogate exists (DOI/PDF/excerpt/scan), use it as the normative source instead of the physical-only book cite. e.g., ACM DOI `https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/<doi>` for ACM papers IS auditable when paywall-free. Secondary aggregator URLs (Wikipedia, `https://pragprog.com/tips/`, `https://martinfowler.com/bliki/<topic>.html`, `c2.com/cgi/wiki`) are VERIFICATION PROXIES only — they help re-verify the primary quote without owning the book physically, but are NOT cited as normative source. **Independent named-reviewer sign-off mandate** *(Round-3 amendment b per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "Lower-confidence reviewer-sign-off mandate" sole-orchestrator framing — sole-orchestrator verification is no longer admissible)*: rule edits citing TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL MUST cite a SECOND verifier-identity BEYOND the orchestrator who replayed the verbatim quote against the source — commit body MUST embed BOTH verifier-identity-1 (the orchestrator, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-05 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`) AND verifier-identity-2 (the independent named reviewer, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-05 by <human-name> against same book + same page + same quote]`) with explicit `[VERIFIED yyyy-mm-dd by <name> against <source>]` markers for each. The 2-verifier requirement closes the "self-attestation only" gap that round-2 left open. **`non-automatable: true` operator-discipline mandate (manual-only; no hook enforcement YET)** *(Round-4 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 SAME-CLASS finding on commit `d07ac71`; supersedes Round-3 amendment c "BLOCKING in T3/T4/T6 verdict-shape" claim that was prose-only without hook implementation — codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE caught the policy/enforcement drift: rule text claimed automated BLOCKING but no T3/T4/T6 hook, verdict parser, schema, or test changed. Per closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md §Outcome A monotone-decline path, downgraded prose closes the drift while the enforcement-hook ship is queued separately)*: when a TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL cite is shipped, the operator MUST: (i) embed `non-automatable: true` marker inline; (ii) embed explicit "no automated enforcement, human gate only" disclosure in commit body acknowledging that automated re-verification is impossible AND naming both verifier-identities (per amendment b); (iii) accept residual provenance gap explicitly. The discipline is OPERATOR-MANUAL — NO T3/T4/T6 hook currently parses `non-automatable: true` as BLOCKING. Promotion to mechanical BLOCKING is FORWARD-REF for a separate enforcement-hook ship: `tools/non_automatable_blocking_audit.py` parsing committed rule edits + emitting BLOCKING status in T3/T4/T6 verdict-shape + regression tests at `tests/test_non_automatable_blocking_audit.py`. Do NOT claim BLOCKING semantic in commit bodies until that ship lands. Forward-only convention codified Wave 18 PSW arc — Bundle B Round-2 commit `d6acfb1`, Bundle B Round-3 commit `217430f`, karpathy 5-author commit `0fe6282`, citation-discipline Round-2 DEMOTE commit `1b87a6e`, citation-discipline Round-3 hard-gate commit `d07ac71`, this Round-4 prose-downgrade commit closes the architectural concern per `reference_wave18_psw_arc_close_4ship_2026_05_04.md` + Outcome A monotone-decline path per `closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md` (R1 conf=0.86 → R2 conf=0.88 ESCALATING → R3 conf=0.82 DECLINING → R4 conf=0.82 SAME-CLASS DECLINING-STABLE; severity stable medium; severity-gate satisfied via concrete-verification mechanism per amendments a+b + prose-downgrade per amendment c; arc converging within Round 5 ceiling).

.\.claude\rules\lga-async-rewake.md:46:**Application** (P1 fix-forward queued from this session's gitnexus debate):
.\.claude\rules\lga-async-rewake.md:48:`gitnexus_pre_edit_impact_guard.py` analyzes blast radius of an Edit/Write operation. The Edit is reversible (git revert); detection-after-Edit is acceptable for advisory purposes. Therefore `async: true, asyncRewake: true` with `GITNEXUS_IMPACT_GUARD_STRICT=1` is the right wire. Currently sync (12s/edit cost from Ship #1 over-correction). NOT codex Option B (drop STRICT entirely — strictly worse, no enforcement on HIGH-impact). asyncRewake provides 0s edit cost + retroactive wake when `impactedCount > threshold (default 10) + GITNEXUS_IMPACT_GUARD_STRICT=1` per gitnexus_pre_edit_impact_guard.py:222-246 — strictly better than both prior options.

.\.claude\rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:115:   - **(c) Lockfile + O_CREAT|O_APPEND atomic-write for SHARED JSONL append**: open the JSONL log with `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | os.O_WRONLY, mode)` where `mode` defaults to `0o600` (owner-only — per Round-5b T3 round-3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS trust-boundary finding on commit `c2b5dee`: `0o644` was world-readable and leaked audit-trail content (agent prompts, PIDs, verdict cite paths, `agent_id` UUIDs, T1/T2/T3 verdict bodies) on multi-user hosts. Callers MAY opt-in to `0o640` group-readable for shared-CI cases via explicit `mode=` argument + documented umask interaction (e.g., `umask 0o027` for CI runner) — `0o644` is REJECTED as default for any audit-trail JSONL). **Migration semantic for legacy files** *(Round-7 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.91 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `df37fb1`; closes non-migrating gap caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE — POSIX `os.open` applies `mode` ONLY when `O_CREAT` actually CREATES the file)*: pre-existing files at `0o644` (created under Round-3-through-5 mandates pre-Round-6) RETAIN their world-readable perms after open, leaving the audit-trail leak intact unless coerced. After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

# Agent harness-fit verification — axis-4 of convergence-gate

# Reference: TIER-2 .claude/projects/Z--claude-sota/memory/feedback_sota_researcher_harness_fit_verification_2026_05_02.md (n=5 promotion-source memory; this rule is the codification per `.claude/rules/codification-threshold.md` cycle-322 jurisdiction n>=3 self-observed promotion bar)
# Reference: TIER-2 .claude/rules/convergence-gate.md (Axis 1+2+3 — this rule adds Axis 4 harness-fit as the scoring layer agents currently miss)
# Reference: TIER-2 .claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md §Subclaim-type discriminator (UPSTREAM-CLAIM / OPERATIONAL-CLAIM / CATEGORY-CLAIM — agents must classify candidate type before harness-fit probe)
# Reference: TIER-2 .claude/rules/codification-threshold.md cycle-322 jurisdiction (n>=3 self-observed promotes feedback→rule; n=5 satisfied)
# Reference: TIER-2 .claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md Must-Never #4 (no duplicate functionality — plugin-namespace duplicates land here as primary class)
# TIER-3 evidence-trail provenance only: `.claude/projects/Z--claude-sota/memory/feedback_sota_researcher_harness_fit_verification_2026_05_02.md` carries the 5-instance evidence ladder + per-class analysis; this rule is the operational mechanism that file's evidence promotes.

## The rule

Sota-researcher / architect / general agent dispatches that surface SOTA candidates MUST include a **harness-fit verification step** asking "is this applicable to OUR specific architecture?" — beyond the convergence-gate Axis 1+2+3 (T1 sources / T2 practitioners / Axis 3 stability) that scores SOTA-status. Without harness-fit, candidates pass convergence-gate AND still fail at ship-target verification because of architectural mismatch invisible to upstream-source-only audit.

This is **convergence-gate Axis 4** (harness-fit) — separate from Axis 1+2+3 (which classify SOTA-status of the candidate ITSELF) and applied AFTER convergence-gate PASS, BEFORE ship-target verification.

## When this rule applies

Whenever an agent (sota-researcher / architect / general-purpose / Explore / code-reviewer / debugger) returns a ship-candidate ranking from a Wave-N dispatch:

1. The agent's convergence-gate verdict is necessary BUT NOT SUFFICIENT for ship-readiness
2. The candidate may be valid SOTA AND inapplicable to claude-sota
3. Apply the 4-axis harness-fit probe BEFORE writing T1 consult prompt OR queuing the ship

## How to apply (4-axis probe)

Before declaring an agent's ship-candidate "ready":

### Probe 1 — count-OVER

If the candidate claims a count delta (commit count, file count, line count, star count): verify against authoritative local source (`git log`, `wc -l`, `Glob | wc -l`, `mcp__github__search_repositories` star refresh) BEFORE accepting. Agent counts via remote APIs can drift, paginate-truncate, or include stale cache.

### Probe 2 — SDK-vs-CLI surface

If the candidate proposes adopting an SDK feature / config flag / env var: verify the **invocation surface** exists in claude-sota:
- Does claude-sota use the SDK or CLI? Check `.claude/hooks/scripts/*.py` + `.claude/settings.json` env block
- Does the candidate's mechanism map to claude-sota's actual mode (interactive vs print-mode vs SDK-managed-agent)?
- If the candidate requires a mode claude-sota doesn't run in, REJECT-for-fit even if SOTA-valid upstream

### Probe 3 — architectural-API

If the candidate proposes a primitive (cache_control, prompt-cache, structured-outputs, batch-API): verify the **API ecosystem match**:
- Anthropic-API primitive vs OpenAI-API primitive vs vendor-neutral OTel
- claude-sota's gpt5.5/codex hooks talk to OpenAI-API endpoints; Anthropic-only primitives don't apply there
- Cross-check before assuming "this Anthropic pattern works on codex"

### Probe 5 — mode-harness-shape

If the candidate proposes adopting a skill/workflow/pattern with operational mode dependencies (HARD-GATE on user interaction, interactive-vs-autonomous mismatch, meta-skill assumptions about sister-harness presence, file-count or size-sprawl orthogonal to existing layout): verify the **operational mode + harness shape match**:
- Does the candidate skill HARD-GATE on interactive user approval? Verify against claude-sota's autonomous /loop mode (incompatible)
- Does the candidate require a sister-skill or sister-harness present in upstream's framework but absent locally? (e.g., Superpowers TDD-for-skills test framework)
- Does verbatim port introduce file count or size disproportionate to existing layer? (e.g., a single skill bringing 7+ files when sibling skills are 1-3 files)
- If ANY mode/harness assumption is unmet, REJECT-FOR-FIT even if SOTA-valid upstream + Axis 1+2+3 PASS

### Probe 4 — plugin-namespace

If the candidate proposes vendoring an artifact from upstream (ECC, codex-plugin-cc, anthropics-cookbook): check **plugin-loaded skill namespace** FIRST:
- `everything-claude-code:<artifact>` exposed via plugin? → DUPLICATE if vendored, REJECT per kiss-dry-yagni Must-Never #4
- `codex:<artifact>` exposed via codex plugin? → DUPLICATE
- `<plugin>:<artifact>` only available as legacy-shim? → still plugin-exposed
- Only proceed with vendoring if the artifact is NOT in any loaded plugin namespace

**Where to check**: the available-skills list injected into agent context via system-reminder (lists every `<plugin>:<skill>` entry). Agents can also `mcp__github__get_file_contents` on the plugin's `marketplace.json` to enumerate exposed commands.

### Probe 6 — supplementary direct-file/registry blockers (FM-09 promotion iter-67)

If the candidate proposes adopting an upstream artifact (skill, MCP server, plugin, library, vendored pattern) whose viability depends on:
- License compatibility (claude-sota is permissive-license-only — MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD acceptable; AGPLv3 / GPLv3 / SSPL / proprietary REJECT)
- README badge / status banner (archive-status, deprecation notice, "moved to maintenance mode" warning)
- Published-package existence (npm / PyPI / cargo / go-modules registry)
- Build-deps availability (Cargo / GCC / Clang / Python venv requirement)

VERIFY via direct-file/registry probes:
- **LICENSE file read** at upstream root: `cat Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/LICENSE | head -5` — match against permissive-license whitelist
- **README badge inspection**: `rg -n "img.shields.io/badge/license|maintenance|archived|deprecated" Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/README.md`
- **Registry direct-existence probe**: `curl -sS https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg-encoded>` (`{"error":"Not found"}` = phantom) OR `curl https://pypi.org/pypi/<pkg>/json` (404 = phantom)
- **Build-deps probe**: `which cargo gcc clang` OR check `pyproject.toml` / `package.json` for unsupported dep stack

If ANY direct-file/registry probe surfaces a blocker, REJECT-FOR-FIT even if SOTA-valid upstream + Axis 1+2+3 PASS + Probe 1-5 PASS. The blocker is STRUCTURAL — no operational mitigation exists.

**Empirical evidence n=2 (FM-09 ladder)**: Memory/RAG audit (openviking AGPLv3 LICENSE blocker — `reference_memory_rag_audit_HNF_agplv3_blocker_2026_05_02.md:52-64`); Ship D (ast-grep MCP phantom @anthropic/mcp-ast-grep npm package — `reference_ship_d_ast_grep_phantom_npm_HNF_2026_05_02.md`).

### Probe 7 — demand-gate split (NEW 2026-05-03; .a/.b sub-class added 2026-05-05 Wave 27 per Agent E §Issue 1 catch-22)

If the candidate proposes adopting a primitive (MCP / skill / library / tool) that is structurally sound (Probes 1-6 PASS): verify the **harness-side operational driver** BEFORE adoption. Probe 7 splits into two outcomes — `.a` REJECT (demand-absence) and `.b` STUDY-PILOT eligible (demand-creates-new-workflow). The split closes the Wave 27 catch-22 surfaced at `tmp/wave27-agentE-saturation-adversarial-2026-05-05.md:46-56,89-106` (Probe 7.a as currently worded auto-REJECTs any primitive that creates a NEW workflow because no sss invocation surface yet exists — circular per Jeffries YAGNI canonical statement at `kiss-dry-yagni.md:31-33`).

**Hard precondition (before applying .a or .b)**: earlier Axis-4 blockers WIN. If the candidate duplicates an existing shipped primitive (Probe 4 plugin-namespace), collides with plugin namespace, requires an unmet harness/mode assumption (Probe 5 mode-harness-shape), fails Probe 6 (license/registry/build-deps blocker), is SUPERSEDED-BY-X (existing primitive owns the workflow), or is a META-HARNESS competing-framework shape per `docs/verified-avoid.md` Cohort 1, classify under that blocker instead. Probe 7.b is ONLY available for structurally sound primitives that create a genuinely new, non-duplicative workflow.

#### Probe 7.a — DEMAND-ABSENCE (REJECT-FOR-FIT)

What sss workflow / invocation surface / consumer would route through this primitive TODAY? Verify the 3-clause check:
- Cite a specific path (existing or queued)
- Is the candidate's value proposition met by an EXISTING shipped primitive? (e.g., "graphiti MCP already provides FalkorDB temporal KG access" → dbhub adds no marginal value AS A REPLACEMENT)
- Is the candidate displacing or extending? Displacement requires migration plan; extension requires marginal-value evidence

If NO current/queued workflow AND .b 5-clause check (below) does not survive, REJECT-FOR-FIT.a (demand-absence) — REJECT-decisive.

#### Probe 7.b — DEMAND-CREATES-NEW-WORKFLOW (STUDY-PILOT eligible)

A structurally sound primitive may create a genuinely new workflow that no existing sss primitive serves. STUDY-PILOT eligibility requires ALL 5 clauses to hold (codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.84 Q2 prescription at `.claude/state/codex_consult_ship27_3_probe7_demand_creates_OUT.txt`):

1. **Named operational use case**: cite the query/workflow and the consumer that would exercise it
2. **Cited local input/source path**: identify the concrete data, repo path, tool surface, or state file (e.g., `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/state/mcp_overhead_audit.jsonl`)
3. **Wiring path**: name the adapter/ETL/config needed to make the primitive consume the source; if wiring is non-trivial, it is part of the pilot cost
4. **Incumbent comparison**: explain why existing shipped primitives or simpler local commands (`rg`, `jq`, GitNexus, Langfuse MCP, graphiti, mcp-memory, one-off Python scripts) do not already satisfy the use case OR are materially worse
5. **Reversible time-box**: define owner, max pilot cost, 30-day success criterion, and retirement path

**Pilot failure**: retire to `disabledMcpjsonServers` if applicable and document in `docs/verified-avoid.md` under the matching failure cohort; create a dedicated retired-pilot / demand-not-realized cohort only after n>=2 same-shape recurrences. NOTE: `verified-avoid.md` Cohort 2 is specifically Probe 6 direct-file/registry blockers per `docs/verified-avoid.md:47-49`; failed demand-pilots do NOT belong there by default. Use the matching failure cohort for retirement (e.g., a pilot that failed because it duplicated an existing primitive retires to Cohort 1 META-HARNESS competing-frameworks).

**Example (dbhub Wave 27 caveat — ETL-explicit)**: bytebase/dbhub could enable SQL analytics over a generated SQLite audit warehouse derived from `.claude/state/*.jsonl`; the pilot must include the JSONL → SQLite ingestion path plus at least one committed query/report consumer. Without that ETL path, dbhub is NOT sufficient evidence for Probe 7.b — DBHub's official surface (`https://dbhub.ai/` + `bytebase/dbhub@72adfdcf` README + `server.json`) supports configured Postgres/MySQL/SQL Server/MariaDB/SQLite databases via SQL tools, NOT direct JSONL querying. Wave 27 codex T1 verified-via codex secondary probe of DBHub introduction page + TOML config docs + GitHub MCP-fetched README/server.json [VERIFIED 2026-05-05 via `.claude/state/codex_consult_ship27_3_probe7_demand_creates_OUT.txt`].

**Harness-fit discriminator for REJECT vs STUDY-PILOT outcomes** (renamed from "4-class harness-fit-FAIL discriminator" per Wave 27 codex T1 Q1 prescription — `.b` is non-fail; original Q3 prescription at `.claude/state/codex_consult_axis4_subclass_taxonomy_probe7_demand_absence_OUT.txt:3825-3829` 2026-05-03; .a/.b split per Wave 27 codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_ship27_3_probe7_demand_creates_OUT.txt` 2026-05-05): use BEFORE classifying a verdict to ensure the right Probe is invoked.

- `DEMAND-ABSENCE.a` (Probe 7.a): no current, queued, or counterfactual workflow survives the named-use-case check — REJECT-FOR-FIT
- `DEMAND-CREATES-NEW-WORKFLOW.b` (Probe 7.b, NON-FAIL CLASS): structurally sound primitive creates a named, non-duplicative workflow; STUDY-PILOT eligible only after the 5-clause check passes
- `SUPERSEDED-BY-X` (related to Probes 4/5): a workflow exists, but an incumbent primitive already owns it or was selected by prior verdict (e.g., cognee → Graphiti L3 verdict)
- `PLUGIN-NAMESPACE` (Probe 4): the artifact already exists in a loaded plugin namespace
- `MODE-HARNESS-SHAPE` (Probe 5): candidate requires an operating mode or harness assumption sss does not satisfy

**Empirical evidence**: n=1 fresh self-observed (bytebase/dbhub REJECT-FOR-FIT 0.85, 2026-05-03 — Agent task output records "no application-DB query workflow"; existing DB-adjacent MCPs cover all live use cases) + n=1 retro corroboration (apollo-graphql per parent `Z:/claude/.claude/projects/Z--claude/memory/reference_mcp_disabled_rationale.md:20`). 4 historical disabled MCPs (claude-context/grafana/opik/local-judge) NOT counted under this Probe — they are CREDENTIAL-GATED-PENDING / A/B-PENDING / SUPERSEDED-BY-X / sss-config-drift distinct classes per the discriminator above.

**Wave 27 caveat (2026-05-05)**: dbhub may be DEMAND-CREATES-NEW-WORKFLOW.b for audit-log SQL analytics, but ONLY with an explicit JSONL → SQLite/Postgres ETL path. DBHub does not currently provide direct JSONL querying. The Wave 27 .b codification specifically opens a pilot pathway IF the operator commits to building the ETL surface — without it, dbhub still falls under Probe 7.a REJECT-FOR-FIT.

Anti-pattern: adopting a primitive because it's SOTA-valid + plugin-namespace-clean + license-compatible WITHOUT identifying a single sss workflow that consumes it. Result is MCP slot occupation without operational driver — historically the disabled-MCP cohort pattern (n=6 in `manifests/services.yaml:80-98` plus `.claude/settings.json:217` `disabledMcpjsonServers`).

Anti-pattern (Probe 7.b bypass — Wave 27 codification): claiming `.b` STUDY-PILOT eligibility for a candidate that fails any earlier Axis-4 blocker (PLUGIN-NAMESPACE / MODE-HARNESS-SHAPE / SUPERSEDED-BY-X / Probe 6 / META-HARNESS competing-framework shape per `docs/verified-avoid.md` Cohort 1). The `.b` escape hatch is admissible ONLY for structurally sound primitives — see Hard precondition above. Without the precondition gate, `.b` becomes a bypass for any attractive new primitive that duplicates `team-lead` / 12-agent fleet / T1-T7 lifecycle / etc.

# Cardinal Rule 12 — Upstream-install-priority over sibling-cite-import

# Promoted from `CLAUDE.md §"NEW Cardinal Rule for this runtime (cardinal-rule-12 upstream-install-priority over sibling-cite-import — Wave 50 fire 10 from user directive 2026-05-06)"` at Wave 160 SB6.

Per prescription #4: paths frontmatter expanded to include "CLAUDE*.md" (CR-12 governs edits to the root memory + cardinal-rule surface, not only manifest/plugin/MCP install surfaces).

# Sister rules: cardinal-rule-9 install-risk discipline (applies at cite-import fallback layer) + cardinal-rule-10 research-first-then-install + cardinal-rule-11 META-process SOTA + cardinal-rule-6 official-native-channel + `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/codex-t1-fix-forward-pattern.md` verdict-shape lattice (mapping shown below) + `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md` Must-Never #4 (DUPLICATE class disposition).

## The rule

12. **Upstream-install-priority over sibling-cite-import.** Every architectural primitive MUST follow source-priority order:
    1. **PRIMARY (default)**: install from upstream SOTA repo via official-native-channel per cardinal-rule-6 (npm / cargo / uvx / `/plugin install` / `gh release download` / `docker pull` / `git clone` from canonical https://github.com URL with HEAD-SHA pin)
    2. **SECONDARY (read-only research)**: cite-anchor TIER-1 SOTA pattern at `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/<file>:<line> @ HEAD <SHA>` — immutable cite consumed as RESEARCH input per cardinal-rule-9 read-only research probe exception; NOT install-class
    3. **TERTIARY (last-resort exception)**: cite-import-AMBER from sibling claude-sota per Section 14.5 — permitted ONLY when sota-researcher subagent invocation per cardinal-rule-10 step 4 returns **HONEST-NON-FINDING evidence** demonstrating no upstream parity exists for the primitive

    **Cite-import-AMBER is NOT DEFAULT.** Manifest rows MUST satisfy the HONEST-NON-FINDING gate predicate before STAGED → CITE-IMPORT-AMBER promotion (testable):
    - (i) sota-researcher subagent dispatched with explicit upstream-parity-probe scope (probe upstream marketplaces / npm / PyPI / cargo / GitHub repos / Anthropic CC docs / ECC plugin skills / mattpocock-skills / obra-superpowers / anthropic-cookbook for primitive equivalent)
    - (ii) Probe DAG (P1 LICENSE → P2 registry-existence → P3 plugin-namespace → P4 GraphQL stars-and-bands → P5 README/frontmatter → P6 deep audit) per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/agents/sota-researcher.md` returns NO install-class equivalent
    - (iii) HONEST-NON-FINDING return shape per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`
    - (iv) Manifest row records HNF evidence (sota-researcher dispatch ID + probes + return) in `docs/install-provenance.md` under `effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` marker per cardinal-rule-1 cite-class lattice (sibling-derived CANNOT be elevated to TIER-1 SOTA per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md` rule #8)

    **CR-9 install-risk discipline applies at the cite-import fallback layer**: pre-cite-import REVERT check + sibling-bleed defense + version-pin (sibling commit SHA at copy time) + 2-round fix-forward budget. The fallback path is NOT free of CR-9; it inherits ALL CR-9 sub-rules.

    **Operational integration with CR-10 + CR-11**: cardinal-rule-10 step 1 ("(a) Install canonical SOTA solution") preempts step (b)/(c)/(d) under CR-12 — research-first-then-install workflow MUST exhaust upstream-install paths BEFORE classifying as cite-adapt OR best-SOTA-recommended OR HONEST-NON-FINDING. Cardinal-rule-11 META-process: every fire involving sibling-cite-import is gated by upstream-parity probe.

    ### CR-12 disposition lattice (6 classes — Wave 134 Fire 27 series + W152-F20+ CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL codification)

    Beyond the **install-source priority order** (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TERTIARY) above, every upstream-vs-incumbent relationship falls into ONE of 6 classes. Wave 134 Fire 27 series mapped 5 (classes 1-5 below); W152-F20+ same-arc n=4 evidence promoted CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL as the 6th (per `codification-threshold.md` cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path):

    1. **GENUINELY-NEW** — no Anthropic/incumbent parallel exists for the primitive's scope. Disposition: **INSTALL via CR-12 PRIMARY path** (official-native-channel per CR-6). No further audit needed beyond Probe DAG.

    2. **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY** — full parallel exists in Anthropic/eee stack covering same scope and mechanism. Disposition: **REJECT-FOR-FIT** per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md` Must-Never #4 (no duplicate functionality without clear reason).

    3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27c_mem0_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.87.

    4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27a_openai_agents_python_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.89.

    5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Pattern B HNF disposition at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27b_langgraph_OUT.txt`.

    6. **CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL** — Anthropic-OFFICIAL educational/reference material (cookbook notebook / official docs / non-runtime / non-install artifact) ALREADY operating as TIER-1 cite reference per existing pin in `research-protocol.md` or equivalent. Distinct from PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT (parallel runtime mechanism) and ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT (core primitive new with ecosystem footprint) by requiring: (a) audited object is REFERENCE material not runtime/install artifact, (b) cite-class adoption is the CORRECT primary mode, (c) correct disposition is RATIFICATION of an existing eee rule/practice against the TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source. Disposition: **ACCEPT-AS-CITE-REFERENCE** — do NOT install as runtime artifact; ratify existing eee discipline against TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source; document operational-overlap for future cite-extraction priority queue. Empirical evidence: W152-F20 + F22 + F23 + F24 (n=4 same-arc 2026-05-11) — Anthropic Cookbook overall (F20 commit `4170fbc`) + CMA prompt-versioning ratified FM-21 OWNED rule (F22 commit `4ed6666`) + CMA human-in-loop ratified CR-7 + safety floor (F23 commit `04b1eb4`) + research-agent recipe ratified sota-researcher + multi-source-discovery-breadth (F24 commit `1d35a22`). **Promotion gate**: n=4 same-arc exceeds `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/codification-threshold.md:34-39,76-80` default n=2 confirmation bar (per cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path: ~3-10 min/audit × ~10-20 educational-source audits/month = ~30-200 min/month savings; LOC ≤200 fit).

    **Cite class for this 6-class lattice itself**: `constituents=[TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ Wave 134 Fire 27-A + 27-B + 27-C codex T1 verdicts, TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ W152-F20 + F22 + F23 + F24 same-arc n=4 evidence (commits 4170fbc + 4ed6666 + 04b1eb4 + 1d35a22), TIER-2 @ existing cardinal-rule-12 scaffolding, TIER-2 @ Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md rule #8 source-class reduction lattice precedent, TIER-1-DIRECT @ Anthropic + OpenAI + LangChain TIER-1 maintainer evidence]; effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md` rule #8 MIN_PRECEDENCE.

    **Application discipline**:
    - When auditing ANY upstream candidate for eee adoption, FIRST classify per 6-class lattice (after Probe DAG passes); THEN apply class-specific disposition
    - Class assignment is determined by **mechanism comparison** vs incumbent (not surface API similarity alone)
    - **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** vs **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY**: distinguished by whether both incumbents cover DIFFERENT scopes (PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT — both useful) or SAME scope (DUPLICATE — pick one)

    - **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** is the OPERATIONAL escape valve when a candidate's core primitive is novel but ecosystem footprint creates duplicate-frameworks concern
    - **CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL** applies ONLY when the audited object itself is educational/reference material (NOT runtime/install artifact); having a cite anchor is NOT sufficient — PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT and ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT candidates can also have parallel cite anchors. The discriminator is "is the object itself an install-class artifact or reference material?"

# SOTA-installed manifest — single source of truth for claude-sota-installed

> **Purpose**: every architectural primitive in `claude-sota-installed` is tracked here with: install or cite-import command + upstream HEAD SHA + axis 1+2+3 verdict + Probe DAG outcome + smoke-probe verification + disposition. >
> **Two install classes** (per user directive 2026-05-06 "all the sources form advanced repos, and guide"):
>
> - **INSTALL-CLASS** — code/binary that RUNS in the runtime (plugin / MCP server / CLI binary / direct .claude/* import / hook script). Lives under `.claude/plugins/cache/` / `.mcp.json` / system PATH / `.claude/{rules,agents,skills,commands,hooks/scripts}/`.
> - **CITE-CLASS** — documentation/guide that authorities a primitive without running. Cited at `<repo>/<file>:<line> @ HEAD <SHA>` in this manifest's "Source guide" column. Examples: CCBP `claude-settings.md`, Karpathy gist, Boris Cherny tips.
>
> Every row carries BOTH classes where applicable (the install + the guide it implements).

## Status legend

- `INSTALLED` — install complete + smoke-probe PASS + axis-1+2+3 verified
- `INSTALLED-VIA-SYSTEM-PATH` — primitive available via system PATH (winget / chocolatey / package-manager-system-scope) at acceptable freshness per cardinal-rule-6; version anchor + smoke probe + axis verdict captured in install-provenance.md (added Wave 50 fire 4 per Agent C-redo P1-3 — fire 3 PATH-discovery introduced this disposition)
- `INSTALLED-AMBER` — install complete but Probe DAG flagged P2/P3 issue; manifest carries the deferred fix
- `CITE-IMPORT-AMBER` — sibling cite-import per Section 14 / 14.5 exception; subagent or hook copied with sibling commit-SHA cite trail; re-evaluate when sibling commit-SHA churns >50% post-import
- `STAGED` — install command run but smoke-probe pending
- `DEFERRED-PENDING-FIX` — install blocked on upstream issue (e.g., breaking change, license incompat); cite-import permitted as substitute pending fix
- `REJECTED-POST-PROBE` — Probe DAG returned REJECT-FOR-FIT or axis-fail; cite-only retained for forward research
- `PLANNED` — design phase; install command drafted but not yet run
- `CITE-ONLY` — guide source cited as authority; no install needed (e.g., CCBP cardinal-rule cites)
